I've farmed this land in Quzhou my whole life, like my father before me. This county is flat North China Plain — good soil, but dry. You have to pump water from the ground or the crop dies. I have 8 mu. My son went to the city years ago, so it's mostly me and my wife now. I hired a neighbor's tractor service to help with the heavy work.

There's really only one thing to decide: wheat in winter, corn in summer. That's what everyone here does. That's what works. I'm not going to try something new at my age — soybeans, cotton, whatever — those are for younger men with money to lose on experiments.

For the wheat, I'll use the improved variety the township extension station pushed a few years ago. The yields were better than my old seed, so I kept buying it. I put down compound fertilizer when I plant, then come back with urea when the wheat is jointing. I irrigate four times: before the ground freezes, at jointing, at heading, and once more when the grain is filling. This dry weather means if I skip a watering, I lose yield. I'll spray herbicide early on and come back once for aphids or rust if I see it.

Right after the wheat comes off in June, I plant corn the same week. I buy hybrid seed from the supply store — whatever they're selling that everyone uses, the 郑单958 type. The summer rains help so I usually only have to pump once if July is dry. I do rotary tillage on the wheat stubble before planting corn. One pesticide pass, maybe none if the season looks clean.
